fields.text: Chooses whether table and EEPROM accesses go to Flash program memory or to data EEPROM.

fields.name: DC2B
fields.text: PWM mode: low two bits of the PWM duty cycle, whose upper eight bits are in CCPR2L. Unused in capture and compare modes.

fields.name: CCP2M
fields.text: Picks the CCP2 operating mode: off, capture, compare or PWM.

values.text: Compare: CCP2 pin driven high and CCP2IF set on match.
Compare: CCP2 pin driven low and CCP2IF set on match.
Compare: CCP2IF set on match, pin left alone.
Compare Special Event Trigger: CCP2IF set, pin left alone, the timer chosen by C2TSEL reset, and ADON set to start an A/D conversion when the A/D is enabled and TRIGSEL is 0.

fields.name: P1M
fields.text: Picks how the enhanced PWM drives its pins. With CCP1M<3:2> = 00, 01 or 10 (capture/compare): xx = P1A is the capture/compare input and P1B, P1C, P1D are port pins. With CCP1M<3:2> = 11 (PWM), half-bridge modules: 0x = single output, P1A modulated, P1B a port pin; 1x = half-bridge, P1A and P1B modulated with dead-band control. With CCP1M<3:2> = 11, full-bridge modules: 00 = single output, P1A modulated, P1B, P1C, P1D port pins; 01 = full-bridge forward, P1D modulated, P1A active, P1B and P1C inactive; 10 = half-bridge, P1A and P1B modulated with dead-band control, P1C and P1D port pins; 11 = full-bridge reverse, P1B modulated, P1C active, P1A and P1D inactive.

fields.name: DC1B
fields.text: PWM mode: low two bits of the PWM duty cycle, whose upper eight bits are in CCPR1L. Unused in capture and compare modes.

fields.name: CCP1M
fields.text: Selects the ECCP1 mode. 0000 = capture, compare and PWM off, module reset; 0001 and 0011 = reserved; 0010 = compare, output toggles on a match; 0100 = capture on each falling edge; 0101 = capture on each rising edge; 0110 = capture on each 4th rising edge; 0111 = capture on each 16th rising edge; 1000 = compare, a match drives the CCP1 pin high and sets CCP1IF; 1001 = compare, a match drives the CCP1 pin low and sets CCP1IF; 1010 = compare, a match sets CCP1IF as a software interrupt and leaves the CCP1 pin alone; 1011 = compare, special event trigger: a match sets CCP1IF, resets the timer and leaves the CCP1 pin alone. PWM, half-bridge modules: 1100 = P1A high-true, P1B high-true; 1101 = P1A high-true, P1B low-true; 1110 = P1A low-true, P1B high-true; 1111 = P1A low-true, P1B low-true. PWM, full-bridge modules: 1100 = P1A, P1C high-true and P1B, P1D high-true; 1101 = P1A, P1C high-true and P1B, P1D low-true; 1110 = P1A, P1C low-true and P1B, P1D high-true; 1111 = P1A, P1C low-true and P1B, P1D low-true.

fields.name: C2TSEL
fields.text: Chooses which timers CCP2 uses.

fields.name: C1TSEL

fields.name: ECCP1ASE
fields.text: Shows an auto-shutdown: 1 = a shutdown event has happened and the CCP1 outputs are held in their shutdown state; 0 = the CCP1 outputs are running. With P1RSEN = 1 the bit clears by itself once the event ends; with P1RSEN = 0 software must clear it to restart the PWM. When C1SYNC or C2SYNC in CM2CON1 is enabled, the shutdown is delayed by Timer1.

fields.name: ECCP1AS
fields.text: Chooses what triggers an auto-shutdown of the ECCP1 outputs.

fields.name: PSS1AC

fields.name: PSS1BD

fields.name: STR1SYNC

fields.name: STR1A

fields.name: P1RSEN

values.text: After an auto-shutdown, ECCP1ASE clears itself when the event ends and the PWM restarts.

fields.name: SMP
fields.text: SPI master: 1 samples input data at the end of the output time, 0 at its middle. SPI slave: keep it 0. I2C master or slave: 1 turns slew-rate control off for standard speed (100 kHz and 1 MHz), 0 turns it on for high speed (400 kHz).

fields.name: CKE
fields.text: SPI master or slave: 1 transmits on the active-to-Idle clock edge, 0 on the Idle-to-active edge. I2C only: 1 switches the input thresholds to SMBus-compliant levels, 0 turns the SMBus inputs off.

fields.name: D/A#
fields.text: In I2C mode, tells whether the most recent byte sent or received was data or an address.

fields.name: P
fields.text: In I2C mode, flags that a Stop condition was the last bus event seen; cleared when SSPxEN is cleared to turn the MSSP off.

values.text: A Stop was the last condition seen; reads 0 after Reset.
The last condition seen was not a Stop.

fields.name: S
fields.text: In I2C mode, flags that a Start condition was the last bus event seen; cleared when SSPxEN is cleared to turn the MSSP off.

values.text: A Start was the last condition seen; reads 0 after Reset.
The last condition seen was not a Start.

fields.name: R/W#
fields.text: In I2C mode, keeps the R/W# bit of the last address match, valid only from that match until the next Start, Stop or not-ACK#. Slave: 1 is a read, 0 a write. Master: 1 means a transmit is under way, 0 that none is; OR it with SEN, RSEN, PEN, RCEN or ACKEN to tell whether the MSSP is idle.

fields.name: UA
fields.text: In 10-bit I2C mode, shows whether the address in SSPxADD needs updating.

fields.name: BF
fields.text: Shows whether SSPxBUF holds data. Receive (SPI and I2C): 1 means a receive finished and SSPxBUF is full, 0 that it has not and SSPxBUF is empty. Transmit (I2C only): 1 means a transmit is under way and SSPxBUF is full, 0 that it finished and SSPxBUF is empty; ACK# and Stop bits are not counted.

fields.name: WCOL
fields.text: Write collision flag. Master: 1 means SSPxBUF was written while the I2C conditions did not allow a transmission to start. Slave: 1 means SSPxBUF was written while the previous word was still going out; software clears it. 0 means no collision.

fields.name: SSPOV
fields.text: Receive overflow flag; software clears it. SPI: 1 means a byte arrived while SSPxBUF still held the last one, and the SSPxSR data is lost; it can happen only in slave mode, where SSPxBUF must be read even when only sending to keep it from being set. In master mode it is never set, since each transfer starts with a write to SSPxBUF. I2C: 1 means a byte arrived while SSPxBUF still held the last one; ignored when transmitting. 0 means no overflow.

fields.name: SSPEN
fields.text: Turns the serial port on or off. SPI: 1 hands SCK, SDO, SDI and SS# to the port; they still need the right input or output direction. I2C: 1 hands SDA and SCL to the port; both must be set as inputs. 0 turns the port off and gives the pins back as I/O port pins.

fields.name: CKP
fields.text: SPI: 1 makes the clock idle high, 0 idle low. I2C slave, SCL release: 1 lets the clock run, 0 holds it low to stretch it for data setup time. Not used in I2C master mode.

fields.name: SSPM
fields.text: Picks the MSSP mode and its clock source. SSPxADD values 0, 1 and 2 are not allowed in I2C mode.

values.text: SPI slave, clock from SCK, SS# control on.
SPI slave, clock from SCK, SS# control off; SS# free as I/O.
I2C master run by firmware (slave idle).
I2C slave, 7-bit address, Start and Stop interrupts on.
I2C slave, 10-bit address, Start and Stop interrupts on.

fields.name: GCEN
fields.text: In I2C slave mode, lets the general call address raise an interrupt.

values.text: Interrupt when address 0x00 arrives in SSPxSR.

fields.name: ACKSTAT
fields.text: In I2C mode, shows whether the other end acknowledged.

fields.name: ACKDT
fields.text: In I2C receive mode, the bit sent when software starts an Acknowledge sequence after a receive: 1 sends Not Acknowledge, 0 sends Acknowledge.

fields.name: ACKEN
fields.text: In I2C master receive mode, 1 starts an Acknowledge sequence on SDA and SCL that sends ACKDT; hardware clears it. 0 means the sequence is idle. It cannot be set, and SSPxBUF cannot be written, unless the I2C module is idle.

fields.name: RCEN
fields.text: In I2C master mode, turns on receive. It cannot be set, and SSPxBUF cannot be written, unless the I2C module is idle.

fields.name: PEN
fields.text: In I2C master mode, 1 sends a Stop condition on SDA and SCL; hardware clears it. 0 means the Stop condition is idle. It cannot be set, and SSPxBUF cannot be written, unless the I2C module is idle.

fields.name: RSEN
fields.text: In I2C master mode, sends a Repeated Start condition. It cannot be set, and SSPxBUF cannot be written, unless the I2C module is idle.

values.text: Send Repeated Start on SDA and SCL; hardware clears it.

fields.name: SEN
fields.text: As I2C master, 1 puts a Start condition on the SDA and SCL lines and hardware clears it; 0 means no Start is pending. As I2C slave, 1 turns on clock stretching for both transmit and receive, 0 turns it off. In master mode it cannot be set, and SSPxBUF cannot be written, unless the I2C module is idle.

fields.name: ACKTIM
fields.text: In I2C mode, shows that the bus is in an Acknowledge sequence; it works only while AHEN or DHEN is set.

values.text: In an Acknowledge sequence; set on the 8th falling SCL edge.
Not in an Acknowledge sequence; cleared on the 9th rising SCL edge.

fields.name: PCIE
fields.text: In I2C mode, turns on the interrupt for a detected Stop condition. No effect in slave modes that already have Start and Stop interrupts on.

fields.name: SCIE
fields.text: In I2C mode, turns on the interrupt for a detected Start or Restart condition. No effect in slave modes that already have Start and Stop interrupts on.

fields.name: BOEN
fields.text: SPI slave: 1 writes every new byte into SSPxBUF whatever BF says; 0 leaves the buffer alone and sets SSPxCON1.SSPOV when a byte arrives with SSPxSTAT.BF already set. With 1, for daisy-chained SPI, SSPOV is still set when a byte arrives with BF = 1, but the newest byte keeps going into SSPxBUF, so all but the last byte can be ignored. I2C master: no effect. I2C slave: 1 updates SSPxBUF and sends ACK# for a received address or data byte regardless of SSPOV, as long as BF = 0; 0 updates SSPxBUF only while SSPOV is clear.

fields.name: SDAHT
fields.text: In I2C mode, sets the least SDA hold time after SCL falls.

fields.name: SBCDE
fields.text: In I2C slave mode, enables bus collision detection: when SDA reads low on a rising SCL edge while the module drives high, PIR2.BCLIF is set and the bus goes idle.

fields.name: AHEN
fields.text: In I2C slave mode, enables holding the bus after a matching address byte.

values.text: After the 8th falling SCL edge of a matching address, SSPxCON1.CKP is cleared and SCL is held low.

fields.name: DHEN
fields.text: In I2C slave mode, enables holding the bus after a received data byte.

values.text: After the 8th falling SCL edge of a data byte, hardware clears SSPxCON1.CKP and holds SCL low.

fields.name: MSK7
fields.text: I2C address mask for received address bit 7.

values.text: Bit 7 is compared with SSPxADD<7> for an address match.
Bit 7 is left out of the address match.

fields.name: MSK6
fields.text: I2C address mask for received address bit 6.

values.text: Bit 6 is compared with SSPxADD<6> for an address match.
Bit 6 is left out of the address match.

fields.name: MSK5
fields.text: I2C address mask for received address bit 5.

values.text: Bit 5 is compared with SSPxADD<5> for an address match.
Bit 5 is left out of the address match.

fields.name: MSK4

values.text: Bit 4 is compared with SSPxADD<4> for an address match.
Bit 4 is left out of the address match.

fields.name: MSK3

values.text: Bit 3 is compared with SSPxADD<3> for an address match.
Bit 3 is left out of the address match.

fields.name: MSK2

values.text: Bit 2 is compared with SSPxADD<2> for an address match.

fields.name: MSK0

fields.name: ADD
fields.text: I2C master: the baud rate divider; the SCL period is ((ADD<7:0> + 1) * 4) / FOSC. 10-bit slave, high address byte: ADD<2:1> hold the top two address bits. 10-bit slave, low address byte: ADD<7:0> hold the low eight address bits. 7-bit slave: ADD<7:1> hold the address.

peripherals.name: EUSART
peripherals.title: Enhanced Universal Synchronous Asynchronous Receiver Transmitter (EUSART)

fields.name: CSRC
fields.text: Picks where the clock comes from in Synchronous mode: 1 = master, the BRG makes the clock; 0 = slave, the clock comes in from outside. Ignored in Asynchronous mode.

fields.name: TX9
fields.text: Chooses a 9-bit or 8-bit transmit frame.

fields.name: TXEN
fields.text: Turns the transmitter on. In Synchronous mode, SREN or CREN takes precedence over it.

fields.name: SYNC
fields.text: Picks synchronous or asynchronous operation of the EUSART.

fields.name: SENDB
fields.text: In Asynchronous mode, a 1 sends a Sync Break with the next transmission and hardware clears it when the Break is done; 0 means the Break has gone out. Ignored in Synchronous mode.

fields.name: BRGH
fields.text: Baud rate speed choice in Asynchronous mode: 1 = high speed, 0 = low speed. Not used in Synchronous mode.

values.text: Handshake off; usual for isochronous endpoints.

fields.name: EPCONDIS
fields.text: With EPOUTEN = 1 and EPINEN = 1: 1 bars endpoint 0 from control transfers, leaving only IN and OUT transfers; 0 lets endpoint 0 take control (SETUP) transfers as well as IN and OUT transfers.

fields.name: EPOUTEN
fields.text: Enables output (OUT) on endpoint 0.

fields.name: EPINEN
fields.text: Enables input (IN) on endpoint 0.

fields.name: EPSTALL
fields.text: Stalls endpoint 0; it has effect only while endpoint 0 is enabled and is ignored otherwise.

fields.name: SOFIF
fields.text: Set when the SIE receives a Start-of-Frame token.

fields.name: STALLIF
fields.text: Set when the SIE sends a STALL handshake.

fields.name: IDLEIF
fields.text: Flags that the bus has stayed Idle for 3 ms or longer; after this, the USB module may be put into Suspend mode.

fields.name: TRNIF
fields.text: Flags that the pending transaction has finished processing, with its endpoint details in USTAT; clearing it moves the USTAT FIFO forward, for IN, OUT and SETUP tokens only.

values.text: Transaction done; endpoint details in USTAT.
Transaction still in progress, or none pending.

fields.name: ACTVIF
fields.text: Flags activity on the D+/D- lines; it is usually unmasked only after a UIDLE interrupt event has been detected.

fields.name: UERRIF
fields.text: Flags that an error condition enabled in UEIE has occurred; it only reports status and software can neither set nor clear it.

fields.name: URSTIF
fields.text: Set on a valid USB Reset, which also loads 00h into UADDR.

values.text: Valid USB Reset seen; UADDR loaded with 00h.

fields.name: SOFIE
fields.text: Enables the Start-of-Frame token interrupt.

fields.name: STALLIE
fields.text: Enables the STALL handshake interrupt.

fields.name: IDLEIE
fields.text: Enables the idle detect interrupt.

fields.name: TRNIE
fields.text: Enables the transaction complete interrupt.

fields.name: ACTVIE
fields.text: Enables the bus activity detect interrupt.

fields.name: UERRIE
fields.text: Enables the USB error interrupt.

fields.name: URSTIE
fields.text: Enables the USB Reset interrupt.

fields.name: BTSEF
fields.text: Set on a bit stuffing error.

fields.name: BTOEF
fields.text: Set on a bus turnaround time-out.

values.text: Time-out: more than 16 bit times of idle passed since the previous EOP.

fields.name: DFN8EF
fields.text: Set when a data field's length is not a whole number of bytes.

values.text: Data field was not a whole number of bytes.
Data field was a whole number of bytes.

fields.name: CRC16EF
fields.text: Set when a CRC16 check fails.

fields.name: CRC5EF
fields.text: Set when a token packet is refused for a CRC5 error.

values.text: Token packet refused on a CRC5 error.

fields.name: PIDEF
fields.text: Set when the PID check fails.

fields.name: BTSEE
fields.text: Enables the bit stuff error interrupt.

fields.name: BTOEE
fields.text: Enables the bus turnaround time-out error interrupt.

fields.name: DFN8EE
fields.text: Enables the data field size error interrupt.

fields.name: CRC16EE
fields.text: Enables the CRC16 failure interrupt.

fields.name: CRC5EE
fields.text: Enables the CRC5 host error interrupt.

fields.name: PIDEE
fields.text: Enables the PID check failure interrupt.

fields.name: FRM
fields.text: Frame number, bits 10:8.

registers.name: UFRML
notes: No figure draws this register; it is read from the register file summary.

fields.name: FRM
fields.text: Frame number, bits 7:0.

registers.name: UADDR
notes: No figure draws this register; it is read from the register file summary.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: USB device address.

registers.name: HLVDCON
registers.title: HIGH/LOW-VOLTAGE DETECT CONTROL REGISTER
notes: The register file summary gives the reset as 00000000.
HLVDL: the maker prints the codes listed; the codes between 1110 and 0000 are shown as dots.

fields.name: VDIRMAG
fields.text: Picks whether the HLVD event fires on a rising or a falling supply against the HLVDL trip point.

values.text: Event when the voltage reaches or rises past the HLVDL trip point.
Event when the voltage reaches or drops past the HLVDL trip point.

fields.name: BGVST
fields.text: Status flag: reads 1 once the internal band gap references have settled.

values.text: Band gap reference not yet stable.

fields.name: IRVST
fields.text: Status flag: shows whether the detect logic is ready to raise its interrupt flag at the chosen voltage range.

values.text: Detect logic will set the interrupt flag at the chosen voltage range.
Detect logic will not set the interrupt flag at the chosen voltage range; leave the HLVD interrupt disabled.

fields.name: HLVDEN
fields.text: Powers the high/low-voltage detect module on or off.

fields.name: HLVDL
fields.text: Sets the voltage detect level, from lowest (0000) to highest (1110); 1111 uses an external analog input on the HLVDIN pin instead.

values.text: Trip input taken from the HLVDIN pin.

fields.name: LS48MHZ
fields.text: Picks the low-speed USB clock: the system clock it assumes and the FS/LS divider that goes with it.

values.text: System clock taken as 48 MHz; FS/LS USB clock divider set to 8.
System clock taken as 24 MHz; FS/LS USB clock divider set to 4.

fields.name: CPUDIV
fields.text: Divides the CPU system clock.

fields.name: CFGPLLEN
fields.text: Turns the PLL on or off.

values.text: Oscillator goes through the PLL, x3 or x4 as PLLSEL picks.
Oscillator passed straight through, no PLL.

fields.name: PLLSEL
fields.text: Picks the PLL multiplication factor.

fields.name: IESO
fields.text: Lets the clock change over from the internal oscillator block to an external oscillator; with FOSC<3:0> on HS, XT or LP and FCMEN = 1, set it too, which avoids a false clock failure and changes over once the OST times out.

fields.name: FCMEN
fields.text: Turns on the Fail-Safe Clock Monitor; with FOSC<3:0> on HS, XT or LP and this bit set, IESO should be set too, which avoids a false clock failure and switches over once the OST times out.

fields.name: PCLKEN
fields.text: Decides whether software may switch off the primary clock.

values.text: Software may turn the primary clock off.

fields.name: FOSC
fields.text: Selects the oscillator type and, for some, CLKO output on OSC2.

values.text: External clock, low power, below 4 MHz.
External clock, low power, below 4 MHz; CLKO on OSC2.
External clock, medium power, 4 to 16 MHz.
External clock, medium power, 4 to 16 MHz; CLKO on OSC2.
External clock, high power, 16 to 48 MHz.
External clock, high power, 16 to 48 MHz; CLKO on OSC2.
HS mode, medium power, 4 to 16 MHz.
HS mode, high power, 16 to 25 MHz.

fields.name: LPBOR#
fields.text: Turns the low-power brown-out reset on or off (active low).

fields.name: BORV
fields.text: Sets the nominal brown-out reset threshold VBOR.

fields.name: BOREN
fields.text: Picks how Brown-out Reset is turned on: by hardware, by software through SBOREN, or not at all. The Power-up Timer is controlled apart from it.

values.text: On, hardware only; SBOREN has no effect.
On in hardware, off in Sleep; SBOREN has no effect.
On, controlled by software through SBOREN.
Off in both hardware and software.

fields.name: PWRTEN#
fields.text: Turns the Power-up Timer on when clear; it is controlled apart from Brown-out Reset.

fields.name: WDTPS
fields.text: Sets the watchdog timer postscaler ratio.

fields.name: WDTEN
fields.text: Chooses whether the watchdog runs by hardware, by the SWDTEN bit, or not at all.

values.text: WDT always on by hardware; SWDTEN has no effect.
WDT switched on and off by SWDTEN.
WDT on while the device runs, off in Sleep; SWDTEN has no effect.
WDT off by hardware; SWDTEN has no effect.

fields.name: MCLRE
fields.text: Gives the pin to MCLR or to the RE3 input.

values.text: Pin is MCLR; RE3 input off.
Pin is the RE3 input; MCLR off.

fields.name: SDOMX
fields.text: Picks which pin carries SDO.

fields.name: T3CMX
fields.text: Picks which pin carries the Timer3 clock input T3CKI.

fields.name: PBADEN
fields.text: Chooses whether the low PORTB pins come out of reset as analog inputs or digital I/O.

values.text: ANSELB<5:0> reset to 1; PORTB<5:0> start as analog inputs.
ANSELB<5:0> reset to 0; PORTB<4:0> start as digital I/O.

fields.name: CCP2MX
fields.text: Picks which pin carries the CCP2 input/output.

registers.name: CONFIG4L
registers.title: CONFIGURATION REGISTER 4 LOW
notes: The register file summary reads bit 0 STRVEN.

fields.name: DEBUG#
fields.text: Turns on the background debugger when clear, giving RB6 and RB7 to in-circuit debug. Debuggers and programmers set it themselves; in normal running it is kept at 1.

values.text: Debugger off; RB6 and RB7 are general purpose I/O.
Debugger on; RB6 and RB7 serve in-circuit debug only.

fields.name: XINST
fields.text: Turns on the extended instruction set and Indexed Addressing mode.

values.text: Extended set and Indexed Addressing on.
Extended set and Indexed Addressing off (Legacy mode).

fields.name: ICPRT
fields.text: Moves in-circuit debug to the dedicated ICD pins. Only on 44-pin TQFP devices; on every other device it is programmed to 0.

values.text: ICPORT on: ICD on the dedicated pins.
ICPORT off: ICD on RB6 and RB7.

fields.name: LVP
fields.text: Turns single-supply ICSP programming on or off.

fields.name: STVREN
fields.text: Decides whether a stack full or underflow resets the device.

fields.name: CPD
fields.text: Code-protects the data EEPROM (active low).

fields.name: CPB
fields.text: Code-protects the boot block (active low).

fields.name: CP3
fields.text: Code-protects flash block 3 (active low). Present on PIC18(L)F45K50 and PIC18(L)F25K50 only.

fields.name: CP2
fields.text: Code-protects flash block 2 (active low). Present on PIC18(L)F45K50 and PIC18(L)F25K50 only.

fields.name: CP1
fields.text: Code-protects flash block 1 (active low).

fields.name: CP0
fields.text: Code-protects flash block 0 (active low).

fields.name: WRT3
fields.text: Write-protects flash block 3 (active low). Present on PIC18(L)F45K50 and PIC18(L)F25K50 only.

fields.name: WRT2
fields.text: Write-protects flash block 2 (active low). Present on PIC18(L)F45K50 and PIC18(L)F25K50 only.

fields.name: WRT1
fields.text: Write-protects flash block 1 (active low).

fields.name: WRT0
fields.text: Write-protects flash block 0 (active low).

fields.name: EBTR3
fields.text: Blocks table reads of block 3 made from code in other blocks (active low). Present on PIC18(L)F45K50 and PIC18(L)F25K50 only.

values.text: Block 3 readable by table reads from other blocks.
Table reads from other blocks are blocked.

fields.name: EBTR2
fields.text: Blocks table reads of block 2 made from code in other blocks (active low). Present on PIC18(L)F45K50 and PIC18(L)F25K50 only.

values.text: Block 2 readable by table reads from other blocks.
Table reads from other blocks are blocked.

fields.name: EBTR1
fields.text: Blocks table reads of block 1 made from code in other blocks (active low).

values.text: Block 1 readable by table reads from other blocks.
Table reads from other blocks are blocked.

fields.name: EBTR0
fields.text: Blocks table reads of block 0 made from code in other blocks (active low).

values.text: Block 0 readable by table reads from other blocks.
Table reads from other blocks are blocked.

fields.name: WRTD
fields.text: Write-protects the data EEPROM (active low).

fields.name: WRTB
fields.text: Write-protects the boot block (active low).

fields.name: WRTC
fields.text: Write-protects the configuration registers when clear. Read-only in normal running; written only in ICSP mode.

registers.name: DEVID2
registers.title: DEVICE ID REGISTER 2
notes: The register file summary gives the reset as 01011100.

fields.name: DEV
fields.text: Upper eight bits of the device ID; with DEV<2:0> in DEVID1 they name the device.

fields.name: DEV
fields.text: Lower three bits of the device ID; with DEV<10:3> in DEVID2 they name the device.

fields.name: REV
fields.text: Silicon revision of the device.

fields.name: EBTRB
fields.text: Blocks table reads of the boot block made from code in other blocks (active low).

values.text: Boot block readable by table reads from other blocks.
Table reads from other blocks are blocked.

fields.text: Turns the WDT on and off from software; acts only when WDTEN<1:0> = 10b.

registers.title: BUFFER DESCRIPTOR n STATUS REGISTER (BD0STAT THROUGH BD63STAT), SIE MODE (DATA RETURNED BY THE SIDE TO THE MCU)

fields.name: UOWN
fields.text: USB own bit; in this view it is 1: the SIE owns the BD and its buffer.

values.text: The SIE owns the BD and its buffer.

fields.name: PID
fields.text: Token PID of the last IN, OUT or SETUP transaction received.

fields.text: BC<9:8>, top two bits of the byte count, written by the SIE with the bytes actually received on OUT or sent on IN.

registers.name: BDnSTAT
registers.title: BUFFER DESCRIPTOR n STATUS REGISTER (BD0STAT THROUGH BD63STAT), CPU MODE

fields.name: UOWN
fields.text: USB own bit: who owns the BD and its buffer; set to the wanted value before the USB module is turned on.

values.text: The core owns the BD and its buffer.

fields.name: DTS
fields.text: Data toggle the packet is expected to carry; only acted on while DTSEN = 1.

fields.name: DTSEN
fields.text: Turns on data toggle checking by the SIE against DTS.

values.text: Toggle checking on; packets with the wrong toggle are dropped, but a SETUP transaction is taken regardless.

fields.name: BSTALL
fields.text: Makes the SIE answer with STALL any token that would use this BD.

values.text: Buffer stall on: STALL sent for a token that would use this BD; UOWN stays set and the BD is left as it is.

fields.name: BC
fields.text: BC<9:8>, top two bits of the byte count to send on an IN token or receive on an OUT token; with BC<7:0> the count runs 0 to 1023.

fields.name: BDnCNT
fields.text: Byte count, low eight bits BC<7:0>; BDnSTAT<1:0> holds the top two.
